A merged PR has no branch left to sync or fix, so its red CI runs are stale. Option B is ruled out because the PR is not open. Option C is ruled out because the PR has nothing that isn't already on main.
Q2: I don't have the PR's job names, failing assertions or run ID: GITHUB FACTS contain only merge state, and I can't read Actions logs. Choosing A would mean promising data I can't supply, which breaks the data-provision guard. B would mean stating job names as fact without evidence. So I'm replacing "both failed jobs on PR #6947 pass" with a check that is at least as strict and can be done on the current default branch (see plan).
Q3: Nothing on the default branch is shown to be broken. The safest reading is that no existing test changes unless an assertion fails when the tests are run against current `main`.
Q4: The PR is merged. If the same test modules pass on current `main`, there is nothing to fix. Adding a test for behaviour that already works (B) widens scope. A human hand-off (C) isn't needed, because no `claude/*` push or sync is required once the branch has merged.

Fix only that confirmed default-branch defect, using the documented behaviour (agents.md "Heal scope from failing tests", the changelog fragment, PR #6947) to decide which side is wrong. Do not rewrite the test just to match the code.

  equivalence_argument: The PR has merged, so its head can't be re-run or re-synced, and its code now lives only on `main`. Running the same CI test modules against current `main` exercises exactly the merged code plus everything that landed after it. That makes it at least as strict as re-running the stale PR jobs.
  reversibility: If someone later produces the original job names and assertions and they point at a module outside this set, a new issue can run that module. No code changes under this decision, so nothing has to be reverted.
